leads.title: Smallpox inoculation in China
leads.why: Blowing powdered scabs into the nose gave the first deliberate immunity to a disease, and the practice was general in China by the seventeenth century.
leads.verify: The earliest reliable Chinese text describing inoculation (the sixteenth-century references, against the unsupported legend of an eleventh-century origin); the nasal method; whether Ottoman and Indian inoculation descend from it or arose apart.

Needham origins of immunology variolation China
history of variolation China India Ottoman

leads.title: Laboratory-attenuated vaccines in France
leads.why: Weakening microbes on purpose turned Jenner's single lucky case into a general method, from which nearly all later vaccines descend.
leads.verify: The dates of the chicken cholera (1879 to 1880), anthrax (1881) and rabies (1885) work; what Pasteur's notebooks show about the methods used at Pouilly-le-Fort and the part of Toussaint and Roux.

leads.title: Clonal selection theory in Melbourne
leads.why: It explained immune memory and self-tolerance and became the framework for monoclonal antibodies, transplantation and modern vaccine design.
leads.verify: Burnet's 1957 paper and its debt to Jerne (1955) and Talmage (1957); the 1958 Nossal and Lederberg experiment showing one cell makes one antibody.
search: Burnet 1957 clonal selection theory Australian Journal of Science
Nossal Lederberg 1958 one cell one antibody
Jerne natural selection theory antibody formation 1955

leads.title: Experimental psychology in Germany
leads.why: Measuring sensation and reaction times in a laboratory made the mind a subject of science and trained the founders of psychology worldwide.
leads.verify: Fechner's 1860 psychophysics; the founding date and work of Wundt's Leipzig laboratory (1879); Ebbinghaus on memory (1885); rival claims for William James at Harvard.

leads.title: Psychotherapy by talking in Vienna
leads.why: The talking cure made conversation a treatment in its own right, and later therapies, including those now tested in trials, grew from it or against it.
leads.verify: Breuer's case of 1880 to 1882 and the 1895 Studies on Hysteria; what was new compared with hypnotic suggestion (Nancy, Paris) and moral treatment; the rise of tested successors such as cognitive behavioural therapy.

origins of psychotherapy hypnosis Bernheim Janet

leads.title: Lithium treatment of mania in Australia
leads.why: A simple salt calmed mania and later proved to prevent relapse in bipolar illness, the first modern drug for a mental disorder.
leads.verify: Cade's 1949 paper and patients; the toxicity problem; Schou's controlled trials in Denmark (1954 onward) that established it.

concepts.name: Laboratory-made vaccine
concepts.summary: Protecting against a disease with a microbe that has been deliberately weakened or killed in the laboratory.

concepts.name: Clonal selection theory of immunity
concepts.summary: The explanation that each immune cell makes one antibody and that an infection selects and multiplies the cells that fit it.

concepts.name: Experimental psychology
concepts.summary: Studying perception, memory and thought by measurement and controlled experiment.

concepts.name: Historical variolation knowledge
concepts.summary: Knowledge of a historical pre-vaccine disease prevention practice.

concepts.name: Drug treatment of mental illness
concepts.summary: Relieving the symptoms of a major mental illness with a drug that acts on them specifically, not by sedation alone.

concepts.name: Psychotherapy
concepts.summary: Treating mental distress through a structured course of conversation with a trained practitioner.
